geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing macro into a courtyard macro so the dominant void becomes spatially central rather than incidental.
Maintain a substantial but not over-open courtyard perimeter to keep the mass compact and capacity-aware.
Align the court opening with the verified access side to create an active street threshold.
Replace the generic clip with a terracing modifier so the upper section participates in a more inhabitable, neighborhood-scaled hierarchy.
Terrace along the long axis to preserve a continuous section rule rather than isolated clipping.
Three terrace steps should clarify the hierarchy without collapsing the mass into excessive fragmentation.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the split-wing emphasis with a courtyard-based massing to create a legible public void and strengthen the neighborhood threshold.
Open the void toward the verified access side to convert the frontage into an active ground response.
Use a moderate courtyard margin to preserve a compact occupied perimeter while still making the void legible.
Shift the roof/upper condition from a clipped lift to a terraced linkage so the section reads as inhabited rather than simply cut.
Orient the terrace-linked section along the long axis to reinforce a continuous upper hierarchy.

rationale: The candidate is coherent enough as a four-view massing and the parcel containment appears respected, but it fails the program fit hard gate for neighborhood living because the dominant split-wing/bridge language reads as a generic sculpted object rather than a clearly active neighborhood ground building. The visible access edge is answered weakly: the blue frontage is adjacent to the mass, but there is no convincing public void, court, notch, or entry seam that clearly activates that edge. The form also looks semantically inconsistent across views, with the split and top notches not resolving into one dominant occupiable idea in plan and section. It does, however, have a reasonably legible primary mass and a coherent overall envelope, so repair integrity is not poor; the main issue is that the section and threshold logic do not yet support the brief. The references suggest two transferable directions: the courtyard/void discipline of the gallery precedent and the strong ground threshold of the cafe precedent. The counterfactual housing precedent indicates that a terraced communal void could work, but the candidate has not yet achieved that inhabited section logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more campus-like and fragmented than this candidate; use the courtyard/void logic, not the overall complexity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Multi-wing rectilinear massing with a clear central void and layered upper setback can support neighborhood-scale mixed use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is more pavilion-like and less spatially distributed than the candidate; do not imitate its flat, singular box language wholesale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact low-rise volume with a strong ground-edge response and a simple attached vertical element can read as neighborhood-serving program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is not achieving the same continuous inhabited section; its split-wing logic is less legible in section and across views.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/stepped massing can produce a strong communal figure when the void and circulation are clearly integrated.
